chapter: Spirits of Rhythm and the road in the 1930s
title: Freelancing and record dates before California
summary: After leaving he freelanced, made records with Jimmy Noone, Frankie Newton and John Kirby's group.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Oh, must have been in the '30s.
Uh-huh. And then you just free
lanced for a couple of years? I just free lanced and got with Duke. I mean, got with -- let's see.
No. I was making records on the side before I left New York, with Jimmy Ke Noone.
And I got out -- come out here and I got to gigging, you know.
Who did you work with? Did you work with somebody steady, though, before you came out here, for a year or so there?
Yeah, with -- I know you made a lot of records with Frankie Newton and --
Well, I was making record dates.
Yeah, I was getting record dates. With some of them old blues players, you know, that come out.
And, let's see -- this is taking me back.
Yeah. Well, it was like John Kirby?
Who started those groups, the groups with Kirby, around that time?
Kirby got his own group together.
Wasn't it Frankie Newton that started the group?
Frankie Newton played with him also, right?
Oh, boy. You're taking me there. You're really taking me. Something else that I can try to think of?
